selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main reassurance is given at the beginning for readers who may struggle with this treatise?
questions.answer: Even if they cannot fully understand everything, they will still gain some benefit from it.

questions.question: What does the comparison with a garden teach about learning from difficult texts?
questions.answer: A reader does not need to master everything to receive meaningful benefit.

questions.question: How does the fruit example help explain different levels of understanding?
questions.answer: It shows that people can take from a text according to their capacity.

questions.question: How does the second reason connect the difficulty of the book to its subject matter?
questions.answer: The book deals with Divine unity in a very broad and deep way, so many readers cannot grasp everything at once.

questions.question: How does the second cause describe the treatment of Divine unity?
questions.answer: It is presented in a highly comprehensive way connected to a supreme divine manifestation.

questions.question: What reading challenge comes from truths that are “great and extensive”?
questions.answer: Explaining them may require very long sentences and extended development.

questions.question: What special spiritual setting is mentioned in the fifth reason?
questions.answer: The insights of the treatise came during Ramadan.

questions.question: In the fourth cause, what makes the discussion feel excessive to some readers?
questions.answer: The repeated presentation of many proofs and demonstrations.

questions.question: In the fifth reason, what time of year is linked with the inspiration for the work?
questions.answer: Ramadan.

questions.question: Why was the text not carefully rearranged afterward?
questions.answer: The writer felt it had come in a way that should not be reshaped by his own later preferences.

questions.question: What does the opening statement say about who can understand the whole treatise?
questions.answer: Not everyone will be able to understand all of it.

questions.question: What lesson about fairness to different readers is built into the garden image?
questions.answer: A work can serve both those who grasp a little and those who grasp much.

questions.question: What does the passage clearly say about the number of reasons for difficulty?
questions.answer: There are five.

questions.question: In the second cause, what makes the subject especially demanding?
questions.answer: It presents Divine unity through a very wide and elevated manifestation, which makes the material deep and expansive.

questions.question: According to the third cause, why is brevity sometimes avoided?
questions.answer: Because shortening the wording might break apart a large truth that needs to remain whole.

questions.question: In the third reason, why is it important not to split up certain truths too much?
questions.answer: Because doing so could damage the wholeness of the meaning being explained.

questions.question: What is one effect of having ten or twenty proofs for a topic?
questions.answer: The explanation becomes extended and harder for some readers to follow.

questions.question: What spiritual source is mentioned in the fifth cause?
questions.answer: The treatise’s lights are said to have come from the blessing of Ramadan.

questions.question: In the fifth reason, what does the mention of Ramadan contribute to the portrayal of the work?
questions.answer: It presents the work as having come through a spiritually blessed period.

questions.question: What two language-related details are given at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: Some Arabic passages remained in the work, and one all-Arabic section was separated into its own work.

questions.question: What balanced view of the treatise is presented in the first paragraph?
questions.answer: It is not fully understandable to everyone, yet it still offers something valuable to every reader.

questions.question: What does the passage say is not possible for all readers?
questions.answer: Fully understanding every matter in the treatise is not possible for everyone.

questions.question: What is the first reason for the difficulty of the book?
questions.answer: It was written from the writer’s own direct understanding and for his own use, not shaped around other people’s ways of thinking.

questions.question: What is distinctive about the author’s method in the first cause?
questions.answer: He wrote from his own observations and understanding rather than tailoring the work to others.
